lines.trans: You would have done better to go calmly into nature.
To go to a quiet forest or a nice park.
Why come to my restaurant for that?
Forgive me, Dima, I wanted to leave in style.
Wait a minute and listen to me carefully.

lines.trans: Well what now, should we shoot ourselves every day?

I really do not need a dead body in my restaurant right now.
Calmly hand over your little pistol here.
At times we no longer have the strength to fight them.
Having solved some problems, we immediately meet new ones.

meanings.en: to sort out, to settle, to deal with

examples.text: Жизнь снова ставит нас перед трудным выбором.
examples.trans: Life once again places us before a difficult choice.

examples.text: Ну, Сеня, ты труп.
examples.trans: Well, Senya, you are a corpse.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.text: Давайте, ребята, сейчас не расслабляемся.
examples.trans: Come on, guys, let us not relax right now.

examples.text: А ты сейчас куда собрался, Сеня?
examples.trans: And where are you going right now, Senya?

examples.text: Максим, извините, что я сейчас вмешиваюсь.
examples.trans: Maxim, forgive me for interfering right now.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'овсем').

examples.text: Они совсем экономят на нашей культуре.
examples.trans: They are completely skimping on our culture.

examples.text: А что, она тебе совсем не нравится?
examples.trans: What, do you not like her at all?

examples.text: Мне новые отношения сейчас совсем не нужны.
examples.trans: I do not need a new relationship at all right now.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('needed').

examples.text: Мне новые отношения сейчас совсем не нужны.
examples.trans: I do not need a new relationship at all right now.

examples.text: Мне новые отношения не нужны.
examples.trans: I do not need a new relationship.

examples.text: Нормальные продукты не нужно тащить домой.
examples.trans: You must not drag good groceries home.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'come on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

related.gloss: to give (the verb it comes from)

examples.text: Хоть продавай теперь наш ресторан.
examples.trans: I might as well sell our restaurant now.

examples.text: Давайте, ребята, сейчас не расслабляемся.
examples.trans: Come on, guys, let us not relax right now.

examples.text: Давай, быстро иди за работу.
examples.trans: Come on, go back to work quickly.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Они сюда слетелись, как коршуны.
examples.trans: They have flocked here like vultures.

examples.text: Потому что нас всех отсюда выгонят.
examples.trans: Because they will kick all of us out of here.

examples.text: Смотри, сюда как раз Катя идёт.
examples.trans: Look, Katya is walking right this way.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'my own', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Давай сюда спокойно свой маленький пистолетик.
examples.trans: Calmly hand over your little pistol here.

examples.text: Он держит своё слово.
examples.trans: He keeps his word.

examples.text: Они строят свои дома.
examples.trans: They are building their houses.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('small').

examples.text: Давай сюда спокойно свой маленький пистолетик.
examples.trans: Calmly hand over your little pistol here.

examples.text: Маленький дом.
examples.trans: A small house.

examples.text: Одна маленькая формальность.
examples.trans: One small formality.

meanings.note: Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'little pistol' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Давай сюда спокойно свой маленький пистолетик.
examples.trans: Calmly hand over your little pistol here.

examples.text: На кухне ресторана всегда есть пистолетик.
examples.trans: In the restaurant kitchen there is always little pistol.

meanings.en: at times, sometimes, now and then
meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'at times, occasionally, sometimes', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Они переругаются и всю свадьбу нам испортят.
examples.trans: They will quarrel and ruin our whole wedding.

examples.text: Иди скорее поработай в зале.
examples.trans: Go and do some work in the dining room.

examples.text: У Макса настоящий талант портить блюда.
examples.trans: Max has a real talent for ruining dishes.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'we', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Да мы сегодня не особо спешим.
examples.trans: We are not in much of a hurry today.

examples.text: Мы всё прекрасно понимаем.
examples.trans: We understand everything perfectly.

examples.text: Мы ещё и поможем продать себя подороже!
examples.trans: We are even supposed to help sell ourselves more expensively!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'already', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Конечно, нашему ресторану нужен хороший хозяин.
examples.trans: Of course, our restaurant needs a good owner.

examples.text: В туалет? Сеня, это уже перебор.
examples.trans: To the restroom? Senya, that is overkill.

examples.text: Костя, я уже устал бегать от проблем.
examples.trans: Kostya, I am already tired of running from problems.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'strength, power, force' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Хозяин должен быть сильный и уверенный.
examples.trans: The owner must be strong and confident.

examples.text: Порой мы уже не в силах с ними бороться.
examples.trans: At times we no longer have the strength to fight them.

examples.text: Сколько сил в этой машине?
examples.trans: How much power does this car have?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with / from', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Наш ресторан всегда остаётся лучшим в Москве.
examples.trans: Our restaurant always remains the best in Moscow.

examples.text: У нас работает команда профессиональных поваров.
examples.trans: A team of professional chefs works here.

examples.text: Здесь всегда продукты самого высокого качества.
examples.trans: There are always products of the highest quality here.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'them', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы всё прекрасно понимаем.
examples.trans: We understand everything perfectly.

examples.text: Там были все мои деньги, понимаешь?
examples.trans: All my money was in there, do you understand?

examples.text: Они сюда слетелись, как коршуны.
examples.trans: They have flocked here like vultures.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to fight / struggle', paired with 'побороться'.

examples.text: Порой мы уже не в силах с ними бороться.
examples.trans: At times we no longer have the strength to fight them.

examples.text: Нужно бороться дальше или просто покориться судьбе.
examples.trans: We must fight on or simply submit to fate.

examples.text: Мы должны бороться за победу.
examples.trans: We must fight for victory.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'having solved', paired with 'решать'.

examples.text: Решив одни проблемы, мы встречаем сразу новые.
examples.trans: Having solved some problems, we immediately meet new ones.

examples.text: Суд решил.
examples.trans: The court has decided.

examples.text: Я решил.
examples.trans: I've decided.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'one', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Макс, ты к нам на свадьбу один придёшь?
examples.trans: Max, will you come to our wedding alone?

examples.text: По всем признакам всё сходится.
examples.trans: By all the signs, everything adds up.

examples.text: По признакам всё точно сходится.
examples.trans: By the signs, everything matches up.

meanings.note: Borrowed via Polish/German from Greek 'problema' (something thrown forward, a task or question).

examples.text: Костя, я уже устал бегать от проблем.
examples.trans: Kostya, I am already tired of running from problems.

examples.text: А остальное — это уже не наши проблемы.
examples.trans: And the rest is no longer our problem.

examples.text: Решив одни проблемы, мы встречаем сразу новые.
examples.trans: Having solved some problems, we immediately meet new ones.

meanings.en: to meet, to greet, to pick up
meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'тречать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to meet, to welcome', paired with 'встретить'.

examples.text: Решив одни проблемы, мы встречаем сразу новые.
examples.trans: Having solved some problems, we immediately meet new ones.

examples.text: Вас и не должны были встречать.
examples.trans: Nobody was supposed to meet you.

examples.text: Он всегда встречает гостей у двери.
examples.trans: He always greets guests at the door.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'разу').

examples.text: А почему сразу именно я должен доставать?
examples.trans: And why do I have to be the one to get it?

examples.text: Решив одни проблемы, мы встречаем сразу новые.
examples.trans: Having solved some problems, we immediately meet new ones.

examples.text: Сразу видно.
examples.trans: You can see it at once.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('new').

examples.text: И на новую мебель для ресторана.
examples.trans: And for new furniture for the restaurant.

examples.text: Тебе понравится моё новое предложение о покупке.
examples.trans: You will like my new purchase offer.

examples.text: Но у меня для вас две новости.
examples.trans: But I have two pieces of news for you.
